1520-much-ado-about-nothing.title: Much Ado About Nothing
1520-much-ado-about-nothing.creator: William Shakspere
1520-much-ado-about-nothing.description: A book by William Shakspere. Much deserved on his part, and equally remembered by Don Pedro: He hath borne himself beyond the promise of his age; doing, in the figure of a lamb, the feats of a lion: he hath, indeed, better bettered expectation than you must expect of me to tell you how.

arxiv-2102-10179.title: Bayesian Functional Registration of fMRI Activation Maps
arxiv-2102-10179.creator: Guoqing Wang, Abhirup Datta, Martin A. Lindquist
arxiv-2102-10179.description: Abstract Functional magnetic resonance imaging (fMRI) has provided invaluable insight into our understanding of human behavior. However, large inter-individual differences in both brain anatomy and functional localization after anatomical alignment remain a major limitation in conducting group analyses and performing population level inference.

arxiv-2110-03268.title: H-integral and Gaussian integral normal mixed Cayley graphs
arxiv-2110-03268.creator: Monu Kadyan, Bikash Bhattacharjya
arxiv-2110-03268.description: Abstract Abstract If all the eigenvalues of the Hermitian-adjacency matrix of a mixed graph are integers, then the mixed graph is called H-integral . If all the eigenvalues of the (0,1)-adjacency matrix of a mixed graph are Gaussian integers , then the mixed graph is called Gaussian integral .

arxiv-2301-00621.title: Data-Driven Optimization of Directed Information over Discrete Alphabets
arxiv-2301-00621.creator: Dor Tsur, Ziv Aharoni, Ziv Goldfeld, Haim Permuter
arxiv-2301-00621.description: A 2023 arXiv research paper by Dor Tsur, Ziv Aharoni, Ziv Goldfeld, Haim Permuter. Directed information (DI) is a fundamental measure for the study and analysis of sequential stochastic models. In particular, when optimized over input distributions it characterizes the capacity of general communication channels. However, analytic computation of DI is typically intractable and existing optimization techniques over discrete input alphabets require knowledge of the channel model, which renders them inapplicable when only samples are available.

arxiv-2301-08755.title: Tidal Distortions as a Bottleneck on Constraining Exoplanet Compositions
arxiv-2301-08755.creator: David Berardo, Julien de Wit
arxiv-2301-08755.description: Abstract Improvements in the number of confirmed planets and the precision of observations implies a need to better understand subtle effects which may bias interpretations of exoplanet observations. One such effect is the distortion of a short period planet by its host star, affecting its derived density. We extend the work of Burton et al.

arxiv-2401-05863.title: Gamma-rays and Neutrinos from Giant Molecular Cloud Populations in the Galactic Plane
arxiv-2401-05863.creator: and Sovan Chakraborty
arxiv-2401-05863.description: Abstract The recent IceCube detection of significant neutrino flux from the inner Galactic plane has provided us valuable insights on the spectrum of cosmic rays in our Galaxy. This flux can be produced either by a population of Galactic point sources or by diffused emission from cosmic ray interactions with the interstellar medium or by a mixture of both.

arxiv-2407-00754.title: WENDY: Covariance Dynamics Based Gene Regulatory Network Inference
arxiv-2407-00754.creator: Yue Wang, Peng Zheng, Yu-Chen Cheng, Zikun Wang, Aleksandr Aravkin
arxiv-2407-00754.description: A 2024 arXiv research paper by Yue Wang, Peng Zheng, Yu-Chen Cheng, Zikun Wang, Aleksandr Aravkin. Determining gene regulatory network (GRN) structure is a central problem in biology, with a variety of inference methods available for different types of data. For a widely prevalent and challenging use case, namely single-cell gene expression data measured after intervention at multiple time points with unknown joint distributions, there is only one known specifically developed method, which does not fully utilize the rich information contained in this data type.

arxiv-2411-16837.title: Class 𝒮 \mathcal{S} superconformal indices from maximal supergravity
arxiv-2411-16837.creator: Ritabrata Bhattacharya 1 , Abhay Katyal 1 and Oscar Varela 1,2,3
arxiv-2411-16837.description: A 2024 arXiv research paper by Ritabrata Bhattacharya 1 , Abhay Katyal 1 and Oscar Varela 1,2,3. We present a new gauging of maximal supergravity in five spacetime dimensions with gauge group containing ISO(5), involving the local scaling symmetry of the metric, and admitting a supersymmetric anti-de Sitter vacuum. We show this maximal supergravity to arise by consistent truncation of M-theory on the (non-spherical, non-parallelisable) six-dimensional geometry associated to a stack of N N M5-branes wrapped on a smooth Riemann surface.

plos-pone-0006984.creator: Rod Dawson, Rany Condos, Doris Tse et al.
plos-pone-0006984.description: PLOS ONE research article. Current treatment regimens for pulmonary tuberculosis require at least 6 months of therapy. Immune adjuvant therapy with recombinant interferon-γ1b (rIFN-γb) may reduce pulmonary inflammation and reduce the period of infectivity by promoting earlier sputum clearance. We performed

pmc-11576390.title: Real-time morphometric analysis of targeted therapy for neuroblastoma cells in monolayer and 3D hydrogels using digital holographic microscopy
pmc-11576390.creator: Sofia Granados-Aparici, Isaac Vieco-Martí, Amparo López-Carrasco, Samuel Navarro, Rosa Noguera
pmc-11576390.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2024). SummaryHigh-risk neuroblastoma (HR-NB) patient treatment is currently insufficient and challenging due to its high clinical, morphological, and genetic heterogeneity as well as the scarcity of available samples for research. We used a gelatin- and silk fibroin-based hydrogel system with cross-linked vitronectin (VN) as an artificial biomimetic three-dimensional (3D) environment to mirror aggressive neuroblastoma (NB) tumors and tested long-term cell response to Cilengitide (CLG).

pmc-11643838.title: M2BPgs-HCC: An Automated Multilectin Bead Array Indicating Aberrant Glycosylation Signatures Toward Hepatitis C Virus-Associated Hepatocellular Carcinoma Prognosis
pmc-11643838.creator: Hiroko Shimazaki, Haruki Uojima, Kazumi Yamasaki, Tomomi Obayashi, Sayaka Fuseya, Takashi Sato, Masashi Mizokami, Atsushi Kuno
pmc-11643838.description: Regular monitoring of patients with a history of hepatitis C virus (HCV) infection is critical for the detection and management of hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC). Mac-2 binding protein glycosylation isomer (M2BPGi) has been used to monitor fibrosis progression and predict HCC. However, HCC prediction based on M2BPGi has not been optimized.

pmc-12374418.title: Primary care pediatricians’ involvement in influenza vaccination campaign in Italy
pmc-12374418.creator: Rosaria Indaco, Francesca Leoni, Costantino Panza, Paolo Giorgi Rossi
pmc-12374418.description: BackgroundIn 2022, the Italian Ministry of Health extended free annual influenza vaccination to all children aged 6 months to 6 years. Since coverage remained low, the Emilia-Romagna region authorized primary care pediatricians (PCPs) to vaccinate both healthy and chronically ill children in 2023, with the aim of increasing vaccine uptake.

pmc-13169608.title: Mis-spliced FMR1 transcripts in human fragile X syndrome neural progenitors and neurons
pmc-13169608.creator: Shaima M Hourani, Kagistia Hana Utami, Sher Li Oh, Maija L Castrén, Mahmoud A Pouladi
pmc-13169608.description: BackgroundFragile X syndrome (FXS) is a neurodevelopmental disorder caused by loss of fragile X messenger ribonucleoprotein (FMRP). In most cases, this results from a CGG expansion exceeding 200 repeats in the 5’ untranslated region of the fragile X messenger ribonucleoprotein 1 (FMR1) gene, known as the “full mutation”.

pmc-13454522.title: Numerical and experimental investigations on the rock-cutting mechanism of cylindrical PDC cutters and the influence of key parameters on cutting efficiency
pmc-13454522.creator: Dongyang Xue, Xingsong Liao, Haijun Zhang, Hua Wu
pmc-13454522.description: Polycrystalline diamond compact (PDC) bits often encounter challenges such as stick–slip, cutter breakage, and low rate of penetration (ROP) when drilling through complex formations with interlayered soft and hard rocks. Cylindrical PDC cutters have demonstrated promising rock-cutting performance in hard formations, offering a new approach for drilling hard and brittle strata.
